title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 65
paragraphs: Cleomenes, eager to take revenge on Demaratus, arranged matters with Leotychides, son of Menares, son of Agis — a man of the same royal house as Demaratus. The condition was this: if Leotychides were installed as king in Demaratus's place, he would join Cleomenes on the campaign against the Aeginetans. Leotychides already had reason enough to hate Demaratus, and the cause was as follows. Leotychides had been betrothed to Percalos, the daughter of Chilon son of Demarmenos. But Demaratus plotted against him and deprived him of the marriage, seizing Percalos himself beforehand and taking her for his own wife. This was the origin of the feud between Leotychides and Demaratus. And now, at Cleomenes's prompting, Leotychides stood up and swore an accusation against Demaratus, claiming that he had no right to the throne of Sparta because he was not truly the son of Ariston. After this formal charge he pressed his suit, recalling the old remark that Ariston had made when his servant came to announce that a son had been born to him: Ariston, counting up the months, had denied with an oath that the child was his. Leotychides seized on this utterance and argued that Demaratus was not Ariston's son and therefore had no right to rule Sparta. As witnesses he produced those Ephors who happened to have been sitting in council with Ariston at the time and had heard him say it.
